key_insight: An expanded DNA methylation classifier substantially improved sarcoma subtype identification and diagnostic confidence across a much larger set of mesenchymal tumors.
clinical_relevance: This tool may help pathologists resolve ambiguous sarcoma cases, support more precise tumor classification, and improve downstream treatment planning.
method: Trained a machine learning classifier on 4,377 DNA methylation profiles spanning 116 tumor sub-classes and 4 control groups.
Validated performance with five-fold nested cross-validation and four independent external cohorts.
Compared classifier predictions with histopathology to assess diagnostic agreement and reclassification impact.
evidence_signal: In validation, the classifier produced predictions in 73% of cases, with 91% matching histopathology; it also showed a 98% class-level accuracy and a Brier score of 0.017 in cross-validation.
watch_item: Implementation still depends on availability of high-quality methylation profiling and careful integration with expert pathology review, especially for cases without a classifier prediction.
paper_title: Advancing sarcoma diagnostics with expanded DNA methylation-based classification
